rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR MANDATORY TRAINING ON HUMAN RIGHTS FOR ALL OFFICIALS AND EMPLOYEES IN THE EXECUTIVE, LEGISLATIVE AND JUDICIAL BRANCHES OF GOVERNMENT INCLUDING GOVERNMENT-OWNE D AND/OR -CONTROLLED CORPORATIONS AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS, AND FOROTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Inclusion of Human Rights Courses in Government Training Programs. All branches of government, including government-owne d and/or controlled corporations (GOCCs) and local government units (LGUs), shall include the study of human rights as an integral part of the education and training of all their officers and employees, giving priority to those units involved in the administration of justice, intelligence work and maintenance of peace and order.  All government-owne d or -financed training institutions shall include in their curricula a regular course on human rights.

rows.abstract: This proposed bill seeks to provide for a comprehensive juvinile system which shall, among other, increase the age of criminal responsibility from nine (9) to twelve (12) years old.>The bill also incorporates the principle of restorative justice whereby the emphasis is on rehabilitation and reintegration rather than retribution for children committing crimes which are punishable by a sentence of six (6) years and below.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE PRESERVATION, REFORESTATION, AFFORESTATION AND SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT OF THE MANGROVE FORESTS IN THE PHILIPPINES, PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: There shall be established and set aside in all coastal areas in each municipality within the Philippines portions of land solely for the preservation, protection, reforestation and sustainable management of magrove forests.  All existing mangrove forests shall automatically from part of the reservation areas.>This proposed measure also penalize the destruction and cutting of magrove tree, as well as dumping of waste products within the reservation areas.>Furtherm ore, the offender shall be required to pay for the expenses that will be incurred to the restoration or rehabilitation of the mangrove areas that wool be damaged or destroyed.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04359

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MAINTENANCE AND SUPPORT OF ELDERLY MEMBERS OF THE FAMILY AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Elderly Support Act of 2001". Children shall maintain and support their father and/or other direct ascendants who are "in need". > Where an elderly member claims to be in need of financial and other support, he/she may, by himself/herself or through a representative of the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) or by counsel, file a petition in court for his/her maintenance and support for any or all of his/her children.> Upon trial, the elderly member shall be represented by a lawyer from the public attorney's office and shall be exempt from all charges and legal fees.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on POPULATION AND FAMILY RELATIONS since 2001-08-21

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING AFFORDABLE HEALTH CARE SERVICES THROUGH THE HEALTH MAINTENANCE ORGANIZATIONS (HMOs), REGULATING THEIR OPERATIONS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The Department of Health, in close coordination with other agencies of the government, is hereby empowered to supervise and regulate the operations of HMOs and all other entities offering health care services that fall under the definition of HMO inaccordance with Section 4, paragraph (g) of this Act. After registering with the Securities and Exchange Commission, said entities shall secure a license to operate as an HMO from the Department of Health. Existing HMOs at the time of the effectivity of this Act shall likewise secure a license to operate from the Department of Health, in accordance with the Transitory Provisions provided herein.> The Department shall issue the license to operate within thirty (30) days from the submission of thhe complete application and requirement prescribed by the DOH and the implementing rules and regulations of this Act.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04666

rows.abstract: The Secretary of the Department of Education, Cutlure and Sports (DECS) is hereby authorized to provide grants to each DECS Regional Office for use by public schools to develop or expand gifted and talented education programs through one or more ofthe following activities.: (1) Professional Development Programs. - The government may use funds to develop and implement programs to address local need for in-service training programs for general educators, specialists in gifted and talented education, administrators, school counselors, or other personnel at the elementary and secondary levels. (2) Technical Assistance - The government may make materials and services available through regional education service centers, universities, collegesor other entities. (3) Innovative Programs and Services - The government may provide funds for formulate challenging, high-level course work to individual students or groups of students in schools and school districts that do not have the resources t

rows.author: B012
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE SALE THROUGH PUBLIC AUCTION OF ALL KINDS OF CONFISCATED SMUGGLED GOODS AND PRODUCTS, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: Our country has continually been beset with problems of graft and corruption committed by personnel of the different departments of our local and national governments. The Bureau of Customs has not been spared by this malady.> There are several activities of the Bureau of Customs that has been identified as one of the sources of graft and corruption. One particular activity of the Bureau of Customs which is mandated by law is the sale through public auction, of confiscated goods by the Bureau of Customs. Through collusion and manipulation between personnel of the Bureau of Customs and certain unscrupulous individuals this has become a rich opportunity for the commission of graft and corruption to the detriment of both the government and thhe citizenry.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2001-08-21

rows.author: B012
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE REGISTRATION, LICENSURE AND PRACTICE OF FOOD TECHNOLOGY IN THE PHILIPPINES, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Our country's food processing industry must be assured of global competitiveness . Filipino manufactured food products should have the chance of being bought when placed side-by-side with their international competitors.> "Food Safety" isa worldwide concern. Without guarantees towards this end, there will be difficulties in ensuring healthy and safe food and achieving global competitiveness . Professionally trained and "licensed" Food Technologists can be a major force in safeguarding product safety through proper implementation of the HACCP (Hazard Anaylsis and Critical Control Point), ensuring healthy and safe food and which is not a requirement in many international food factories.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-08-21

rows.abstract: The retirement benefits provided under Republic Act No. 910, as amended, are hereby extended to the lawyers in the Public Attorney's Office (PAO) of the Department of Justice, provided that the retirement age for PAO lawyers shall remain at sixty-five years, and that for one who would avail of optional retirement, he shall have attained the age of sity years and has rendered at least twenty years service in the Government, the last five of which shall have been continuously rendered in the Public Attorney's Office.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-08-21

rows.author: B012
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXEMPTING (P50,000.00) SAVINGS DEPOSITS AMOUNTING TO FIFTY THOUSAND PESOS OR LESS FROM WITHHOLDING TAX, AMENDING SECTION 21 (C)(1) OF THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE THEREBY AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Small Deposits Exemption Law". Upon the passage of this law, all Savings Deposits in any banking or quasi-banking institutions amounting to FIFTY THOUSAND PESOS (P50,000.00) or less shall be exempted from withholding taxes as required by the National Internal Revenue Code. >The beneficiaries of this bill are the poor in the society. It seeks to equalize the purchasing power between the rich and the poor by not unduly depriving them of the use of the interests which their deposited money earnsfrom the banking system.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2001-08-21

rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2001-08-22

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING THAT BRAIN TUMOR OR BRAIN CANCER BE CONSIDERED AS AN OCCUPATIONAL DISEASE
rows.abstract: Brain tumor or brain cancer contracted by an employee in the course of or during his employment shall be considred an occupational disease for purpose of securing disability/pens ion benefit and medical or related benefits: Provided, that for the sickness and the resulting disability or death to be compensable, proof must be shown that the risk of contracting the same is brought about or increased by the nature of the employment or by working conditions. > Any doubt as to the compensability ofthe brain tumor or brain cancer  so contracted by the employee during the course of his employment shall be resolved in his favor.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2001-08-22

rows.title_full: AN ACT EXPRESSLY RECOGNIZING THE CANON LAWS OF THE ROMAN CATHOLIC CHURCH, AS WELL AS THE LAWS OF OTHER CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS ORGANIZATIONS OR DENOMINATIONS
rows.abstract: Realizing the significance of the "equal protection clause" of the constitution, it shall be the declared policy of the State to recognize the Canon Laws of the Roman Catholic Church, as well as the laws of other Christian religious organizations ordenominations including the Moslem religion registered under and by virtue of existing laws, pertaining to the marriage contracted in the country or elsewhere. > Pursuant to this policy of the State, a marriage hereinafter declared to be null and void by the Roman Catholic Church or its matrimonial tribunal, and or any duly authorized officer of any other Christian religious organization or denomination including the Moslem religion shall be considered null and void by the State.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2001-08-22

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO EXPAND THE POWERS, DUTIES AND FUNCTIONS OF A PUNONG BARANGAY, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 389, CHAPTER 3 OF THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The duties and functions of the PUNONG BARANGAY shall INCLUDE the following: (1) ENFORCE ALL LAWS AND REGULATIONS RELATING TO THE PREVENTION, USE AND SALE OF ILLEGAL DRUGS; (2) PERFORM MINOR REPAIR AND MAINTENANCE OF MUNCIPAL AND BARANGAY ROADS IN COORDINATION WITH THE MAYORS OF THEIR RESPECTIVE MUNICIPALITIES OR CITIES; AND (3) CONDUCT ANNUALLY A CENSUS OF THE POPULATION OF BARANGAY AND SUBMIT THE RESULT OF SUCH CENSUS TO THE NATIONAL CENSUS STATISTICS OFFICE THROUGH THE MAYOR OF SUCH MUNICIPALITY OR CITY.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-08-22

rows.abstract: The penalty of [prision mayor in its medium period with temporary absolute disqualificatio n or a fine of Six Thousand Pesos] RECLUSION PERPETUA shall be imposed if the maintainer, conductor or bunker of said gambling schemes is a government official, or where such government official is the player, promoter, referee, umpire, judge , or coach  in case of game fixing, point shaving and machination.

rows.abstract: Rationale: The bill lessens the number of cases that a judge will undertake in the court of law. Approval of this bill will enable to devote more time and exerts more valuable efforts to concentrate on more significant cases pending in their salas.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A SEPARATION BENEFIT TO GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS AND EMPLOYEES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: This bill seeks to resolve the inequality by officials and employees of the government who are separated from the service through not fault  of their own but as a result of reduction in force for lack of work or funds, or for a change inthe scope or nature of an agency's program or abolition of an agency or office or its functions and acitivities integrated with those of another agency. > this refers to an official or employee who has rendered at least TEN (10) years or LESS than twenty (20) years of service in the government.

rows.title_full: AN ACT EXPANDING THE COVERAGE OF THE EMPLOYEES COMPENSATION AND STATE INSURANCE FUND TO INCLUDE RETIRED EMPLOYEES AGED SEVENTY (70) AND BELOW WHO SUBSEQUENTLY REAQUIRED EMPLOYMENT, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AS AMENDED

rows.abstract: Coverage in the State Insurance Fund shall be compulsory upon all employers and their employees not over [sixty (60)] SEVENTY (70) years of age; Provided, that an employee who is over sixty (60) years of age and paying contributions to qualify for the retirement or life insurance benefits administered by the system shall be subject to compulsory coverage.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE POSSESSION OR USE OF MOBILE OR CELLULAR TELEPHONE BY CONVICTED PRISONERS AND INDIVIDUALS WHILE INCARCERATED AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: Just recently, it was reported in newspapers that unannounced inspections conducted by officials of penal facilities revealed that some prisoners serving sentence in the national penitentiary and detained persons in city jails were foundto have in their possession cellular phones which they used to contact persons and associates outside the jail where they are confined. The unrestricted use of mobile phones had enabled convicted drug traffickers to direct the operation of their nefarious trade from within the confines of their jail cells, a task almost impossible to perform without these high-tech telecommunicati on gadgets.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-08-22

rows.abstract: Some of the amendments proposed in this bill are as follows: (1) Composition of the NLRC from [fourteen (14)] to TWENTY-THREE (23) members; (2) The Commission may sit en banc or in [five (5)] EIGHT (8) divisions; (3) THE COMMISSION AND ITS EIGHT (8)DIVISIONS SHALL BE ASSISTED BY THE LABOR ARBITRATION OFFICERS IN ITS APPELLATE AND ADJUDICATORY FUNCTIONS WHOSE TERM SHALL BE CO-TERMINUS WITH THE COMMISSIONERS WITH WHOM THEY ARE ASSIGNED. THE LABOR ARBITRATION OFFICERS SHALL BE MEMBERS OF THE PHILIPPINE BAR, THEY SHALL RECEIVE ANNUAL SALARIES AND SHALL BE ENTITLED TO THE SAME ALLOWANCES AND BENEFITS AS THOSE FALLING UNDER SALARY GRADE TWENTY SEVEN (SG 27). THERE SHALL BE AS MANY LABOR ARBITRATION OFFICERS AS MAY BE NECESSARY FOR THE EFFECTIVEE AND EFFICIENT OPERATION OF THE COMMISSION BIT IN NO CASE LESS THAN THREE (3) ASSIGNED TO THE OFFICE OF THE CHAIRMAN AND EACH COMMISSIONER; and (4) Labor Arbiters shall have the SAME allowances, retirement and other benefits as that of the judges of

rows.title_full: AN ACT RATIONALIZING RELIEFS FROM AND EXECUTION OF FINAL DECISIONS AND AWARDS OF THE NATIONAL LABOR RELATIONS COMMISSION AND THE LABOR ARBITERS THEREBY AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLES 223 AND 224 OF THE LABOR CODE
rows.abstract: This bill contains AMENDMENTS to the Labor Code, as follows: (1) Article 223 - APPEAL > IN CASE THE EMPLOYER SHALL OPT FOR PAYROLL REINSTATEMENT, THE EMPLOYEE SHALL PAID HIS SALARIES/WAGES DURING THE PENDENCY OF THE APPEAL IN THE COMMISSION. > IN CASE A MOTION FOR RECONSIDERATION IS FILED, THE DECISION SHALL BE EXECUTORY AFTER TEN (10) CALENDAR DAYS FROM RECEIPT OF THE RESOLUTION OF SUCH MOTION. (2) Article 224 - EXECUTION OF DECISIONS, ORDERS OR AWARDS OF THE COMMISSION SHALL BE UNAPPEALABLE AND REVIEWABLE ONLY BY THE SUPREME COURT ON CERTIORARI UNDER RULE 65 OF THE  RULES OF COURT SOLELY ON QUESTIONS OF LAW OR JURISDICTION.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05944

rows.author: D072
rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7432, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE `SENIOR CITIZENS ACT,' AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: ANY PERSON, FIRM, CORPORATION, ASSOCIATION OR ENTITY WHO SHALL VIOLATE THE [Violation of any] provisions of this Act AND/OR  ANY RULES OR REGULATIONS ISSUED THEREUNDER for which no penalty is specifically provided under any other law, shall UPON CONVICTION, be punished by imprisonment OF NOT LESS THAN THREE (3) MONTHS BUT NOT MORE THAN ONE (1) YEAR [not exceeding one (1) month], or a fine OF NOT MORE THAN TWENTY THOUSAND PESOS (20,000.00) [not exceeding One Thousand Pesos (P1,000.00)], or both,IN THE DISCRETION OF THE COURT: PROVIDED, THAT IN THE CASE OF A CORPORATION , FIRM, PARTNERSHIP OR ASSOCIATION, THE SAME PENALTY SHALL BE IMPOSED UPON ITS OFFICIALS FOR SUCH VIOLATION.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05987

rows.author: D005
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE DEPARTMENT OF FISHERIES AND OCEANS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: All in all, our aquatic territory totals 220,842,253 hectares, more than seven times our land territory which is only 30 million hectares. The vastness of the Philippine time maritime zone and its rich resources dictates that we should have a marine-based economy. In spite of this reality, it is ironic that we do not have a department whose primary purpose is to concentrate on and service the needs of the fisheries sector.> We need  a department that has the muscle to see to it thatour laws and rules are followed, our corals are protected, and a few rich fishermen are prevented from totally scraping our fishing grounds to the detriment of the small fisherfolks.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT REORGANIZATION since 2001-08-22

rows.author: C039
rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE OLD-AGE PENSION OF WORLD WAR II VETERANS, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6948 AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: A World War II veteran shall be paid an old-age pension monthly for life, unless he is actually receiving a similar pension for the same considertion from other government funds or from the United States government. The amount of the monthly old-agepension shall be according to the veteran's age as shown below:  AGE; Monthly Old-Age Pension 65-69 years  -- Five Thousand Pesos (P5,000.00); 70-74 years -- Ten Thousand Pesos (P10,000.00); 75-79 years -- Fifteen Thousand Pesos (P15,000.00); 80-89years -- Twenty Thousand Pesos (20,000.00); 90 above   -- Thirty Thousand Pesos (P30,000.00.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on  since 2001-08-22

rows.author: C039
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING NATIONAL CEMETERIES AND PROVIDING FOR THEIR ADMINISTRATION AND MAINTENANCE
rows.abstract: There shall be established at least one (1) National Cemetery in each Region and major island to serve as a memorial and final resting place for veterans, military personnel and citizens who have rendered distinguished service to the nation. > The President of the Philippines shall establish each National Cemetery by individual Presidential Proclamation which shall set aside a portion of government land for the purpose.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on  since 2001-08-22

rows.author: C039
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7837, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS `AN ACT GRANTING PERMANENT RESIDENT STATUS, OTHER RIGHTS AND PRIVILEGES TO FILIPINO VETERANS OF WORLD WAR II WHO ACQUIRED AMERICAN CITIZENSHIP UNDER THE UNITED STATES IMMIGRATION ACT OF 1990,AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Clarifying the Coverage of of RA 7837, Residency Status to Filipino Veterans who Acquired American Citizenship
rows.abstract: Any Filipino veteran of World War II who acquired American citizenship pursuant to the United States Immigration Act of 1990 OR ANY OTHER PRIOR ACT shall be qualified for permanent resident status and is hereby granted limited property rights and privileges shall likewise automatically accrue upon illigitimate, and unmarried children of Filipino veterans who thereafter acquired American citizenship.> The amendment also shall cover LAND OWNERSHIP and the PRACTIVE OF PROFESSION.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2002-05-23, transmitted to on 2002-05-28 and received by the Senate on 2002-05-28

second_reading.remarks: The Body approved to consider the Explanatory Note of the Bill as the sponsorship remarks.

rows.author: C039
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6948 AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7696
rows.abstract: Rationale: Under the present law , the veterans of World War II are placed on an equal footing with the other categories of veterans in terms of benefits administered by the Philippine Veterans Affairs Office (PVAO).> this system has proven to be prejudicial to the World War II veterans in terms of budgetary allocation for payment of their benefits. The World War II veterans are fast diminishing in number. They deserve the government's special attention in terms of allowing them enjoy their benefits to the full, for the duration of their remaining few days in this world.> This bill, therefore, proposes the amendment of R.A. No. 6948 as amended by R.A. No. 7696 to provide for the grant of the Total Administrative Disability Pension to Worldd War II veterans only.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on  since 2001-08-22

rows.author: C039
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO FURTHER AMEND REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6948, AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7696, TO PROVIDE EQUITY IN THE BENEFITS FOR SENIOR MILITARY VETERANS
rows.abstract: Rationale: Section 5 (h) of Republic Act No. 6948, as amended by Republic Act No. 7696, provides that upon reaching seventy (70) years of age, a veteran/retiree , with or without any service connected disability, shall be considered a totally disabled veteran. The clear intention is to provide an additional benefit to a veteran/retiree upon his reaching seventy (70) years of age. > This provision places a disabled veteran/retiree with actual service connected disability rating at a disadvantagein relation to a veteran who has no service connected ability.> The amending of this provision will remove the inequity by clearly providing that each veteran/retiree upon reaching the age of seventy (70), shall receive the administrative disabilityy pension in addition to his service connected disability pension he is presently receiving.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on  since 2001-08-22

rows.author: C039
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING A LUMPSUM BENEFIT AND OTHER ASSISTANCE SERVICES TO SURVIVORS OF WORLD WAR II VETERANS WHO HAVE DIED PRIOR TO THE ENACTMENT OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6948, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: Dependent of World War II veterans who have died prior to the enactment of Republic Act No. 6948, as amended, shall be granted the following benefits and assistance services: (1) A lump-sum benefit amount to P30,000.00; (2) Hospitalization , medicalcare and treatment at the Veterans Memorial Medical Center following the provisions of Section 15, Republic Act No. 6948, as amended; and (3) A Philippine flag to honor the deceased veteran. > "Dependents" for this purpose refer to the surviving spouses or children following the law of succession.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on  since 2001-08-22

rows.author: C039
rows.title_full: AN ACT FURTHER AMENDING CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6948 OTHERWISE KNOWN AS `AN ACT STANDARDIZING AND UPGRADING THE BENEFITS FOR MILITARY VETERANS AND THEIR DEPENDENTS,' AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7696
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to allow the benefits granted or unclaimed during the lifetime of a decesed veteran to accrue to his or her heirs according to the law on succession. Many veterans, have died even before enjoying their benefits. It is also true that should the veterans have enjoyed such benefits, it was so for just a considerably short period of time, as most of them were already in their twilight years. It is, thus, just and fair for the Government to give importance and recognition to our veterans even when they have already passed away, by way of extending their benefits to their rightful heirs.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on  since 2001-08-22

rows.author: D058
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A COLLEGE EDUCATION TRUST FUND FOR CHILDREN OF GSIS AND SSS MEMBERS
rows.abstract: There is hereby established in the Government Service Insurance System and the Social Security System a special trust fund called the "College Education Trust Fund" to ensure the college education of the children of the Members of both System. > Theamount of premium to be paid to the College Educaiton Trust Fund by the Member shall be, in accordance with the schedule of payments to be provided by the System concerned taking into consideration certain criteria.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06641

rows.author: D058
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZ ING THE OPEN LEARNING SYSTEM IN THE PHILIPPINES APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: To effectively respond to the need for working people to acquire formal higher education and a better professional career and to cater to the demand for continuous education, the establishment of an Open Learning System is therefore proposed by this bill > The idea of establishing an Open Learning System arose from a desire to democratize and expand higher educational opportunities for the people, in a more effective and economical manner. The Open Learning System will utilize the distance teaching/learni ng system, where students shall not be required to regulary attend conventional classrooms, thus allowing these students to study while working in offices, factories, farms or other preoccupations.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2001-08-22

rows.author: D058
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING MOVIE, TELEVISION AND RADIO PRODUCERS INCLUDING PROMOTIONS AND ADVERTISING AGENCIES AND OTHER LIKE ENTITIES WHICH EMPLOY UNEMANCIPATED MINORS TO DEPOSIT THEIR TALENT FEES OR INCOME IN A TRUST FUND, PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR THE VIOLATION OF THE SAME AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: All movie, television, radio producers, including promotions and advertising agencies, talent promoters, and other like entities, who in the course of business hires, procures, or engage the services of an unemancipated minor below eighteen  (18) years of age shall be required to deposit in the name of the said minor at least fifty (50%) percent of the minor's income or talent fee at a bank duly licensed by the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas in the form of a trust fund. > The trust fund established by the immediately preceeding section shall be held in safekeeping by that bank, to earn legal interest, unti the minor shall have reached the age of majority as defined by law, in which case the latter shall be free to handle the deposit as he deeems equitable under the premises.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC INFORMATION since 2001-08-22

rows.author: D058
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLE 192 OF THE CHILD AND YOUTH WELFARE CODE SO AS TO EXTEND ITS BENEFITS TO YOUTHFUL OFFENDERS CONVICTED OF OFFENSES PUNISHABLE BY DEATH OR LIFE IMPRISONMENT OR CONVICTED BY MILITARY TRIBUNALS
rows.abstract: If after hearing the evidence in the proper preceedings, the court should find that the youthful offender has committed the acts charges against him, the court shall determine the imposable penalty, including any civil liability chargeable against him. However, instead of pronouncing judgment of conviction, the court upon application of the youthful offender and if it finds that the bast interest of the public as well as that of the offender will be served thereby, may suspend all further proceedings and commit such minor to the custody or care of the Department of Social Welfare and Development, or to any training institution operated by the government or any other responsible person until he shall have reached twenty-one years of age, orr for a shorter period as the court may deen proper, after considering the reports and recommendations of the Department of Social Welfare and Development or the government training institution or responsible person under whose care he has been commi
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2001-08-22

rows.author: D058
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO IMPROVE THE ADMINISTRATION OF JUSTICE BY DECRIMINALIZING AND PROVIDING FOR THE IMPOSITION OF ALTERNATIVE PENALTIES SHORT OF DEPRIVATION OF LIBERTY FOR CERTAIN OFFENSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Many of the cases that occupy the attention and energies of our police, prosecutors, judges, and prison authorities relate to minor offense, infractions that cause little or no damage to persons, property, and community and those not motivated by malice but by some psychological disorders that call for treatment instead of punishment.> This bill, therefore, seeks to provide innovative measures to improve the administration of justice and reduce the dely in court proceedings. Offensesproposed to be DECRIMINALIZED are stated in this bill.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-08-22

rows.author: D058
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A SYSTEM OF ABSENTEE VOTING BY QUALIFIED FILIPINOS ABROAD
rows.abstract: All Filipinos abroad who are, or have previously been, registered voters in the Philippines, not otherwise disqualified by law, at least eighteen (18) years of age on the day of election, may vote in all national elections for president, vice-president, senators, and party-list representatives in their temporary residence abroad.
rows.status: Substituted by HB03570

rows.author: D058
rows.title_full: THE EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY ACT OF 2001
rows.abstract: Rationale: A survey of existing laws reveals the lack of comprehensive legislation which touch on undue discrimination against women, members of certail religious, regional or ethnic groups, the elderly, homosexuals, and disabled. Sometimes, even Filipinos workers are discriminated in their own country on account of their race. > Aside from the broad pronouncement in the Labor Code, no further protection is provided against discrimination on the basis of race or creed. There appears to be an absence of laws which afford protection for the other marginalized groups.> This bill seeks to expand the coverage of legal protection against discrimination on the basic of the above attributed from the time of pre-employment and labor relations and ppromotion to supervisory and managerial positions. It also provides the mechanisms for the implementation of the same.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-08-22

rows.author: D058
rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING PENSIONS UNDER THE SOCIAL SECURITY SYSTEM, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 12 OF THE SOCIAL SECURITY ACT OF 1997
rows.abstract: Notwithstanding the preceding paragraph, the minimum MONTHLY pension shall be [One thousand two hundred pesos (P1,200.00) formembers with at least ten (10) credited years of service and Two thousand four hundred pesos (P2,400.00) for those with twenty (20) credited years of service] THREE THOUSAND PESOS (P3,000.00): PROVIDED, THAT IN THE SUCCEEDING YEARS STARTING JANUARY, 1999, SAID THREE THOUSAND MONTHLY PENSION BENEFIT SHALL BE INCREASED ANNUALLY BY FIVE HUNDRED PESOS (P500.00) PER MONTH UNTIL (P5,000.00) PER MONTH: PROVIDED, FURHTER THAT THE COMMISSSION SHALL EQUITABLY ADJUST THE MONTHLY PENSIONS OF OTHER ENTITLED MEMEBERS OR BENEFICIARIES WHOSE MONTHLY PENSIONS ARE HIGHER THAN THE MINIMUM MONTHLY PENSION HEREBY ESTABLISHED TO PRESERVETHE INTEGRITY OF THE PENSION PROGRAM.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2001-08-22

rows.author: D058
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE PHILIPIINE OVERSEAS WORKERS BANK, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to further enhance the investment potentials of overseas workers while at the same time aims to address their financial needs and concerns. It provides for the establishment of a banking institution for Filipino overseas workers, tobe known as the Philippine Overseas Workers Bank, to augment their income-generati on capabilities as investors thereof. Added to this, it enjoins the government to provide the necessary financial assistance that will tremendously sustain the validity of the proposed bank.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BANKS AND FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES since 2001-08-22

rows.author: D058
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING INCOME EXTENDERS TO PUBLIC ELEMENTARY AND HIGH SCHOOL TEACHERS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill shall apply only to public elementary and high school teachers in the active service. Certain INCOME EXTENDERS proposed are: (1) Fare discounts; (2) Price discounts on rice and corn; (3) Lower rates of loan interests; (4) Free tuition andmatriculation fees for their children; and (5) Preference in receiving educational loans.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-08-22

rows.author: D058
rows.title_full: AN ACT REDUCING THE RETIREMENT AGE OF GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES, AMENDING FURTHER FOR THE PURPOSE THE 'GOVERNMENT SERVICE INSURANCE SYSTEM ACT OF 1997,' AND FOR OTHER  PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill states that retirement shall be compulsory for an employee at SIXTY (60) years of age, with at least TWELVE years of service. THOSE WHO ARE SIX-ONE YEARS OF AGE SHALL BE RETIRED ON THE THIRD YEAR OF IMPLEMENTATION.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-08-22
